feed-is-connection.statement: Each feed is a connection between the NSS and the SIEM, and a configured NSS server is required to add an NSS feed.

quotes: Feed Name: Enter or edit the name of the feed. Each feed is a connection between the NSS and your SIEM.
NSS Server: Select an NSS server from the list. A configured NSS server is required to add an NSS feed.

siem-fqdn.statement: A TCP feed's SIEM destination can be given as an FQDN: the NSS re-resolves the FQDN only when the existing connection goes down, allowing failover from one IP to another by updating the DNS entry. The feature cannot be used for DNS-based load balancing.

quotes: This allows failover from one IP to the other without manual intervention, but rather relying on updating the DNS entry. The NSS re-resolves the FQDN only when the existing connection goes down. This feature cannot be used for DNS-based load balancing.

siem-rate.statement: SIEM Rate should be left as Unlimited unless the output stream must be throttled due to licensing or other constraints; a limit must be between 100 and 1,000,000, and one that is too low for the traffic volume causes log loss.

quotes: SIEM Rate: Leave as Unlimited, unless you need to throttle the output stream due to licensing or other constraints.
This number must be between 100 and 1,000,000. A limit that is too low for the traffic volume causes log loss.

tcp-output-types.statement: A TCP web feed's output is a comma-separated (CSV) list by default, with Tab-separated as an alternative and feed output types for specific SIEMs in the same menu. The Firewall feed article says Name-Value Pairs or Tab-separated can be chosen if the SIEM accepts them.

quotes: Feed Output Type: The output is a comma-separated (CSV) list by default. Choose Tab-separated to create a tab-separated list.
This menu also lists feed output types for specific SIEMs.
You can choose Name-Value Pairs or Tab-separated if your SIEM accepts any of these formats.

http-enable.statement: In addition to TCP-based feeds, NSS logs can optionally be streamed to a SIEM over HTTP connections, and the AWS guide lists `nss configure-nssas` among the steps to add HTTP-based feeds. Self-signed or internally issued certificates that pass the SIEM connectivity test can also be used only after they are configured in the VM instance.

quotes: In addition to TCP-based NSS feeds, you can optionally stream NSS logs to SIEM over HTTP connections. To add HTTP-based NSS feeds, you must:
nss configure-nssas
Self-signed or internally issued certificates that pass the SIEM connectivity test can also be used only after you configure them in your VM instance.

http-destination.statement: An HTTP feed takes an API URL, the HTTP/S URL of the SIEM log collection API endpoint, HTTP header values such as a token, and a Max Batch Size, a size limit for an individual HTTP request payload to the SIEM's best practice.

quotes: Max Batch Size: Enter a size limit for an individual HTTP request payload to the SIEM's best practice.
API URL: Enter the HTTP/S URL of the SIEM log collection API endpoint.
Value 1: Enter the token value for the HTTP header.

http-json.statement: An HTTP web feed's Feed Output Type says the output is JSON, and Tab-separated is also offered. When JSON is selected, JSON Array Notation is enabled by default, which orders individual logs in a list separated by commas and surrounded by square brackets, and the article says the setting can be disabled.

quotes: Feed Output Type: The output is JSON.
Choose Tab-separated to create a tab-separated list.
JSON Array Notation: When JSON is selected, the JSON Array Notation setting is enabled by default.
Individual logs are ordered in a list, separated by commas, and surrounded by square brackets
You can disable this setting.

cloud-settings.statement: A Cloud NSS web feed has a SIEM Type chosen from a list and a JSON output by default.

quotes: SIEM Type: Choose a SIEM type from the list.
Feed Output Type: The output is JSON by default.

http-self-signed-command.statement: In the HTTP Firewall, HTTP SaaS Security and HTTP Sandbox Verdict NSS feed articles, a self-signed certificate is configured by running `nss add-cert-to-trust <self-signed certificate>` in the VM instance, with the path of the certificate from the NSS node in place of the placeholder.

quotes: To configure a self-signed certificate, run the following command in your VM instance:
nss add-cert-to-trust <self-signed certificate>
Replace <self-signed certificate> with the path of your self-signed certificate from the NSS node in the command.
To configure a self-signed certificate, run the following command in your VM instance:
nss add-cert-to-trust <self-signed certificate>
Replace <self-signed certificate> with the path of your self-signed certificate from the NSS node in the command.
To configure a self-signed certificate, run the following command in your VM instance:
nss add-cert-to-trust <self-signed certificate>
Replace <self-signed certificate> with the path of your self-signed certificate from the NSS node in the command.

http-prerequisite.statement: The HTTP Firewall, HTTP SaaS Security and HTTP Sandbox Verdict NSS feed articles each say that before configuring HTTP NSS feeds, the tasks for the virtual appliance in the NSS Deployment Guides for the platform must be completed.

quotes: Before you start configuring HTTP NSS feeds, complete the tasks for your virtual appliance using the NSS Deployment Guides for your platform.
Before you start configuring HTTP NSS feeds, complete the tasks for your virtual appliance using the NSS Deployment Guides for your platform.
Before you start configuring HTTP NSS feeds, complete the tasks for your virtual appliance using the NSS Deployment Guides for your platform.

status-default.statement: The HTTP Firewall, Cloud DNS, HTTP SaaS Security and Cloud Posture Management feed articles each say a new feed's Status is Enabled by default and can be set to Disabled to activate it at a later time; the wording is "It is Enabled by default", "The NSS feed is Enabled by default" or "The Cloud NSS feed is Enabled by default" depending on the article.

quotes: Status: It is Enabled by default. Click Disabled if you want to activate it at a later time.
Status: It is Enabled by default. Click Disabled if you want to activate it at a later time.
Status: The NSS feed is Enabled by default. Choose Disabled if you want to activate it at a later time.
Status: The Cloud NSS feed is Enabled by default. Select Disabled if you want to activate it at a later time.

output-types-by-log-type.statement: The Feed Output Type wording differs by article. The HTTP Firewall article says the output is JSON and Name-Value Pairs or Tab-separated can be chosen if the SIEM accepts them; the Cloud DNS article says JSON by default with the same two choices; the HTTP SaaS Security article says JSON, with Tab-separated, Custom (a different delimiter such as a dash) and output types for specific SIEMs in the menu; the Cloud Posture Management article says JSON by default, with Tab-separated or Custom.

quotes: Feed Output Type: The output is JSON. You can choose Name-Value Pairs or Tab-separated if your SIEM accepts any of these formats.
Feed Output Type: The output is JSON by default. You can choose Name-Value Pairs or Tab-separated if your SIEM accepts any of these formats.

Feed Output Type: The output is JSON. Choose Tab-separated to create a tab-separated list. Choose Custom to use a different delimiter, such as a dash, and enter the delimiter when you specify the feed output format. This menu also lists feed output types for specific SIEMs.

Feed Output Type: The output is JSON by default. Select Tab-separated to create a tab-separated list. Select Custom to use a different delimiter, such as a dash, and enter the delimiter when you specify the Feed Output Format.

siem-rate-http-cloud.statement: The HTTP Firewall and Cloud DNS feed articles say the SIEM Rate Limit (Events per Second) is only applicable if Limited is selected under SIEM Rate, must be between 100 and 1,000,000, and that a limit too low for the traffic volume causes log loss. The Cloud Posture Management article says the same about a too-low limit.

quotes: SIEM Rate Limit (Events per Second): This is only applicable if you selected Limited under SIEM Rate.
This number must be between 100 and 1,000,000.
A limit that is too low for the traffic volume causes log loss.
SIEM Rate Limit (Events per Second): This is only applicable if you selected Limited under SIEM Rate.
This number must be between 100 and 1,000,000.
A limit that is too low for the traffic volume causes log loss.

cert-by-kind.statement: The HTTP Firewall article says the HTTPS URL can be configured with a publicly trusted SSL certificate and that self-signed or internally issued certificates that pass the SIEM connectivity test can also be used only after they are configured in the VM instance; the Cloud Firewall article says the HTTPS URL must be configured with a publicly trusted SSL certificate, that self-signed or internally issued certificates do not pass the SIEM connectivity test, and that OAuth 2.0 Authentication is enabled by default if it is applicable to the SIEM type.

quotes: The HTTPS URL can be configured with a publicly trusted SSL certificate.
Self-signed or internally issued certificates that pass the SIEM connectivity test can also be used only after you configure them in your VM instance.
The HTTPS URL must be configured with a publicly trusted SSL certificate. Self-signed or internally issued certificates do not pass the SIEM connectivity test.
OAuth 2.0 Authentication: This setting is enabled by default if it is applicable to the SIEM type.

mcas-fixed.statement: An MCAS NSS feed is a connection between the NSS and MCAS; its SIEM IP Address is the local host IP address, pre-populated and not editable, and its Feed Output Format fields are pre-populated and cannot be edited. An NSS virtual appliance deployed before the Internet Access (ZIA) 5.6 release needs the latest version of Java installed in its VM.

quotes: Each feed is a connection between the NSS and MCAS.
SIEM IP Address: This is the local host IP address to stream logs from the NSS to MCAS. The field is pre-populated and cannot be edited.
Feed Output Format: These are the fields that display in the output. The fields are pre-populated and cannot be edited.
If you deployed an NSS virtual appliance before the Internet Access (ZIA) 5.6 release, ensure you have the latest version of Java installed into your VM.

settings-by-kind.title: Which settings each feed kind has
settings-by-kind.detail: Comparing the web-log articles for TCP, HTTP, Cloud NSS and MCAS showed that only the TCP feed has a SIEM IP/FQDN with a TCP port and a Duplicate Logs setting; HTTP and Cloud have an API URL, HTTP headers, Max Batch Size and JSON Array Notation; only Cloud has SIEM Type and OAuth 2.0 and no NSS Server field; MCAS has no SIEM Rate and no editable output format. These are absences seen by diffing articles and cannot be quoted, so they are not claimed.
settings-by-kind.blocks: saying whether a given setting exists for a feed kind

output-types-not-offered.title: Output types the HTTP and Cloud feed articles do not offer
output-types-not-offered.detail: The Firewall and DNS articles offer no Custom delimiter, and the SaaS, DLP, Sandbox, App Governance and Posture articles offer no Name-Value Pairs; only the two SaaS articles mention SIEM-specific output types. Whether the missing types exist for those log types is not stated. The Terraform zia_cloud_nss_feed doc lists nss_feed_type values but was not extracted for this report.

siem-rate-range-other-logs.title: SIEM Rate range on DLP, Sandbox, App Governance and Posture feeds
siem-rate-range-other-logs.detail: The HTTP and Cloud Endpoint DLP, Email DLP and Sandbox Verdict articles and the Cloud 3rd-Party App Governance and Posture Management articles say a limit too low causes log loss but give no 100 to 1,000,000 range. The HTTP Email DLP article words the Limited condition as "This field is available only if you select Limited in the SIEM Rate field." Whether the same range applies is not stated.

max-batch-size.title: Max Batch Size unit, default and range
max-batch-size.detail: The HTTP and Cloud NSS articles say to enter a size limit for an individual HTTP request payload to the SIEM's best practice, with no unit, default or range.

siem-types.title: Cloud NSS SIEM types and OAuth 2.0 applicability
siem-types.detail: The Cloud NSS articles do not list the SIEM types or say which of them use OAuth 2.0. The OpenAPI /nssFeeds surface, the Terraform zia_cloud_nss_feed schema and the SDK models were not checked for this report.

http-cloud-duplicate-logs.title: What an HTTP or Cloud NSS feed replays after an outage
http-cloud-duplicate-logs.detail: No HTTP or Cloud NSS feed article showed a Duplicate Logs setting when diffed against the TCP article. What is replayed to an HTTP or Cloud SIEM after an outage, beyond the one-hour batch retry, is not stated.
